newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo sees U.S. Puregon approval in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Akzo sees U.S. Puregon approval in Q3.

text.p: Chemical group Akzo Nobel NV said on Thursday it had started sales of its new fertility drug Puregon in France and was expecting to gain registration in the United States in the third quarter.
"We hope to gain registration in the most important country, the United States, in the very near future," finance director Jean den Hoed told a results news conference.
"I expect that when we hold the third quarter news conference I can say we have gained (U.S.) registration," he added.
Ultimately, Akzo aimed to gain a 50 percent share of the one billion guilder world market for fertility drugs, Den Hoed said.
"We have as a target of 50 percent of the world market (and) have started introducing Puregon in various smaller countries," Den Hoed said.
Once Akzo had gained registration in the U.S., Puregon sales were expected to take off at the same speed as those of Remeron, Akzo's new anti-depressant which is selling well, he said.
